motion.name: ease-out-quint
motion.purpose: Default easing for all state transitions. Exponential ease-out, no bounce, no elastic. System intent for future animate passes.

motion.name: duration-fast

narrative.overview: TalQ is a worn leather field notebook, not a glass dashboard. Surfaces are soft, warm, and paper-like. Chrome stays low-contrast and recedes so the conversation is the only thing that asks for attention. The mood is unhurried and human: a tool you keep open all day without it raising your pulse. Depth is conveyed by warm tonal layering, never by drop shadows or glass. The system runs on a deliberate tension: the surface is quiet (Field Notebook calm, content-first) while the controls are tactile and confident (real presence, unambiguous affordance). A calm page, a pen that feels solid in the hand. It explicitly rejects generic Material/AI-slop, the default Nextcloud Talk web UI, and the cold-blue chat-app category reflex.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, paper-like surfaces tinted toward umber-black, never neutral gray
A single teal signal accent used sparingly against ink and newsprint
Flat by default; depth only from a four-step warm tonal ladder
Type and spacing carry the hierarchy; ornament is near-zero

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Teal covers at most ~10% of any screen. It marks exactly one thing: this needs you (unread, active, primary action). If two teal things compete on screen, one is wrong.

rules.name: The No-Gray Rule
rules.body: There is no neutral gray anywhere. Every surface, text, and divider value is tinted toward the umber/newsprint hue. A value that reads as gray is a bug.

rules.name: The Two-Lever Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is built from exactly two levers, size and weight (400 vs 600). No italics for hierarchy, no third weight for chrome, no color-as-hierarchy.

rules.name: The Scale Honesty Rule
rules.body: The scale tops out at 16px. Do not fake editorial presence by bolding 14px text. A headline needs a real larger size, not heavier body text.

rules.name: The Flat-Paper Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest, always. Forbidden: box-shadow on cards, panels, rows, bubbles, or dialogs. Depth is a tonal-ladder choice, never a shadow.

rules.name: The Ladder Rule
rules.body: A surface is raised by moving exactly one step up the ladder (base to sidebar to raised to surface). Never skip a step or raise by shadow.

dos: Do keep Signal Teal under ~10% of any screen. Its scarcity is the design.
Do tint every neutral toward umber/newsprint. Pure or cool gray is a bug.
Do build hierarchy from size and weight only.
Do raise surfaces one step up the warm tonal ladder, never with a shadow.
Do give every control its full style on the control itself, immune to ancestor stylesheets.
Do honor reduced-motion and user font scaling, and keep dark and light at WCAG AA contrast.
donts: Don't use #000 or #fff anywhere, including the light-theme surface (current pure #ffffff light bgSurface is a standing fix, not a precedent).
Don't add box-shadow, glassmorphism, blur, or gradient text to any surface.
Don't use a colored side-stripe (border-left/right > 1px) as an accent on rows, bubbles, or callouts.
Don't drift toward generic Material or AI slop: cold gray neutrals, purple-on-white gradients, cookie-cutter identical card grids, templated component kits.
Don't settle for parity with the default Nextcloud Talk web UI; the visible craft gap is the point.
Don't regress toward the cold-blue chat-app category reflex (Slack/Teams clutter, Discord neon-on-charcoal).
Don't fake editorial presence by bolding 14px text in place of a real larger size.
